html:
Roman general and dictator, the first Roman to march on Rome with his own army.

He came from an old but poor noble family. Serving under Marius, he captured Jugurtha in 105 BCE to end the Jugurthine War, and he did well in the Social War. As consul in 88 BCE he was given the war against Mithridates VI of Pontus. When a law moved the command to Marius, Sulla led his legions into Rome and took it back.

In the east he sacked Athens in 86 BCE and forced Mithridates to make peace. He returned in 83 BCE and won a civil war against the followers of Marius, helped by young Pompey and Crassus.

As dictator he posted lists of enemies who could be killed for a reward, the first proscriptions, and seized their property. He tried to give power back to the Senate: he doubled its size, curbed the tribunes and fixed the order of offices. Then, unusually, he gave up power, retired to Campania and died in 78 BCE. His example of taking Rome by force was not forgotten by Julius Caesar, who had escaped his proscriptions as a young man.
sum: Roman general and dictator, the first Roman to march on Rome with his own army.
